slot.brief: Ask which of the given mixtures will show positive/negative deviation from Raoult's law, or what the vapour composition will be above a given liquid mixture — conceptual with a numeric percentage or a qualitative pick.

stem: Among the following liquid pairs, which one shows negative deviation from Raoult’s law?

verdicts.working: Phenol and aniline form stronger intermolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions with each other, giving a negative deviation from Raoult’s law. The other pairs are ideal or show positive deviation.

working:
Negative deviation occurs when A–B intermolecular forces are stronger than A–A and B–B, lowering vapour pressure. Phenol and aniline form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O–H···N and N–H···O) → negative deviation. Benzene–toluene and n-hexane–n-heptane have similar interactions → nearly ideal. Ethanol–cyclohexane: ethanol’s H-bonds are broken, only weak London forces between unlike molecules → positive deviation.

Independent check: Phenol and aniline form stronger intermolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions with each other, giving a negative deviation from Raoult’s law. The other pairs are ideal or show positive deviation.
solution: Negative deviation occurs when unlike-molecule attractions are stronger than like-molecule attractions, lowering vapour pressure. Phenol and aniline form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, such as $\mathrm{O-H\cdots N}$ and $\mathrm{N-H\cdots O}$, so their mixture shows negative deviation from Raoult’s law.
